newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends steady as weather factors offset.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends steady as weather factors offset.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed little changed with concern about the impact of heavy rains on this year's soft red winter crop offset by favorable weather in winter white and hard red winter areas, dealers said.
Dealers noted weekend rains in Ohio, where the soft red winter crop is in the flowering stage, could lead to problems with fungal diseases.
But both the Pacific Northwest (winter white) and the Kansas/Nebraska (hard red winter) area received crop boosting rains over the weekend.
"In both those areas they've got pretty much all their needs for moisture. All in all the weather is more of a negative," said Everen Securities analyst Joel Karlin.
Improved prospects for hard red winter and concern about soft red winter conditions sparked inter-market spreading centering on buying CBOT wheat/selling KCBT wheat.

Dealers noted USDA reported wheat export inspections, for the week to May 29, totalled 9.41 million bushels, up from 6.96 million the previous week. The total was much as expected with trade estimates ranging from seven to 11 million bushels.
July wheat closed 1/4 cent higher at $3.60-3/4 a bushel. Other months were up 1/4 cent to down three cents.
Pit sources said featured buyers included LIT (2.0 million bushels July) while selling was scattered.
Futures volume was estimated at a modest 17,000 contracts, unchanged from Friday.
